verdict.rationale: Gide is a law firm, but it states it uses AI in delivering its services (gide-supp-legaltech), so a client could fairly ask whether their data is used to train AI models. Nothing in the pack describes a training opt-out, a no-training commitment, or how client data is handled in its AI tools. The GDPR advisory practice is a service for clients, not a control over Gide's own data use, so it is not credited.
